examples.knowledge_point: Finding Particular Solutions of Differential Equations by First Rearranging and Then Separating
examples.problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\cos(3y)\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x} + \sin(2x) = 0$ given that  $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0.$ Assume that $-\dfrac{\pi}{6} < y < \dfrac{\pi}{6} .$
examples.worked_solution:
We first find the general solution, and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) \\ \int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3y)\,\text{d}y & =-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3y) & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+C \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3y) & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+{C}_{1}\,,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_1=3C.$

Now let's apply the condition $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0$ to find $C_1\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0) & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})+{C}_{1} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(0) & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+{C}_{1} \\ 0 & =0+{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{1} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So we get the particular solution in implicit form:

$$
\sin(3y)   =  \dfrac {3} {2} \cos(2x)
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the particular solution to the differential equation
$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=4x\sqrt{y}$
that satisfies the condition $y(1)=9.$  Assume that $y>0.$

$y(x)=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find the particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4x\sqrt{y} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\,\text{d}y & =4x\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\,\text{d}y & =\int 4x\,\text{d}x \\ 2\sqrt{y} & =2{x}^{2}+{C}_{1} \\ \sqrt{y} & ={x}^{2}+\frac{{C}_{1}}{2} \\ y & ={({x}^{2}+\frac{{C}_{1}}{2})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Assuming $y>0,$ the general solution is

$$
y(x)=({x}^{2}+C)^{2},
$$

where $C=\frac{{C}_{1}}{2}$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now apply the condition $y(1)=9$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =((1)^{2}+C)^{2} \\ 9 & =(1+C)^{2} \\ 3 & =1+C \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
y(x)=({x}^{2}+2)^{2}.
$$
